notes: Spec asserts: state stays working through the queued message's ARRIVAL, no →ready flicker when the queued input lands, and the cycle still ends at ready. Hermes writes no transcript file — one shared SQLite store at $HERMES_HOME/state.db — so the daemon derives state by folding the session's `messages` rows (metrics.go) and only promotes an assistant row to turn_done on finish_reason='stop' (parser.go). A queued-but-unconsumed message never reaches that store: both of hermes' queue paths put the payload into the CLI's in-process `_pending_input` queue.Queue and nothing calls SessionDB.append_message until the turn loop actually consumes it. So during the arrival window message_count does not grow, no activity event fires for the injection, LastEventType stays assistant_message/tool_result, and the session holds working. The recipe first sends `/busy queue` because hermes' shipped default busy_input_mode is `interrupt`, under which a mid-turn Enter REDIRECTS the running turn instead of queueing it; then it sends a ~600-word prompt and injects a plain follow-up 8s later. session_birth is anchored UNPINNED to recording start so the transient proc-<PID> presession the process scanner mints cannot steal identity and cascade failures; turn_start (working) can only match the store-backed session (<YYYYMMDD>_<HHMMSS>_<hex>) because a presession row never goes working, and it establishes the session identity every later phase chains off. queued_window holds for 10000 ms from turn_start so the asserted no-flicker window genuinely SPANS the +8s injection — stronger than the claudecode/opencode anchors, whose 3000 ms windows stop short of their own injection point. The queued message is then consumed as a NEW turn (the process loop drains _pending_input after turn 1 returns), so the legal inter-turn ready falls outside the window; turn_end matches the FINAL ready. Whether the queued text is folded into the running turn or consumed as a follow-up turn is NOT asserted — both shapes finish in ready. Observations are pinned from the live surface, not from docs: model gpt-5.6-luna appears on every recent source='cli' row in the live store and matches model.default in config.yaml, and cost is priced by irrlicht's capacity table (gpt-5.6-luna carries real pricing there) because Hermes reports estimated_cost_usd=0.0 under billing_mode='subscription_included'.

text: A hermes session appears in ready shortly after launch (the proc-<PID> presession, or the store-backed session if it lands first — left unpinned on purpose)
The first (long) user prompt drives the store-backed session ready → working. Only the real session can match: a proc-<PID> presession row never goes working

A second user message is typed into the REPL 8s into the turn and queued. State must stay working on the same session across the arrival — no flicker to ready when the queued input lands, no flicker to waiting (spec bullets 1 and 2)
The cycle eventually ends at ready (spec bullet 3) once the queued message is consumed — hermes drains it as a follow-up turn, but a fold into the current turn would finish in ready just the same
